section_summary: Correspondence between the State Department and Paterson’s Industrial Commission concerns Japanese silk textile imports, export pricing, and their effect on American manufacturers. A comparison of Japanese and American fabric prices accompanies the commission’s appeal, while later State Department replies direct pricing concerns to the occupation authorities. The section also includes a Tokyo report and press release on higher Japanese raw silk prices, followed by a sparse filing page and an apparently unrelated transmittal to London.

subfiles.title: Conclusion of State Department letter on Japanese exports and the American silk textile industry
subfiles.from: Edward W. Doherty, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Discusses Japan’s need for dollar earning exports and the possible effect of exchange rates on silk prices.
subfiles.summary: The concluding page argues that Japanese exports support economic recovery and reduce dependence on United States funds.

subfiles.title: Reply to Charles H. Roemer on imports of Japanese silk textiles
subfiles.from: Paul H. Nitze, for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains occupation export policy and responds to a proposed embargo on Japanese silk textiles.
subfiles.summary: Nitze says Japan needs export income and that an embargo conflicts with United States trade policy. He states that occupation authorities use floor prices and invites Roemer to submit evidence of unfair competition to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Cover letter forwarding the Industrial Commission’s appeal
subfiles.about: Forwards a letter to Senator Hawkes concerning the Paterson silk industry.
subfiles.summary: Requests the Secretary of State’s prompt reaction to the enclosed appeal.

subfiles.title: Industrial Commission letter to Senator Hawkes on Japanese silk cloth prices
subfiles.about: Argues that Japanese woven silk is priced too low for American manufacturers to compete.
subfiles.summary: The commission disputes Colonel Walker’s account of a gray market, describes price comparisons with American fabrics, and says imports threaten a revived domestic silk industry. It asks Hawkes to recommend revised SCAP prices.

subfiles.title: Schedule comparing Japanese and American silk fabric prices
subfiles.about: Compares SCAP prices with American manufacturers’ quotations for three silk fabrics.
subfiles.summary: Lists specifications and prices for twill habutae, plain habutae, and fuji fabrics.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Roemer’s November appeal
subfiles.from: Charles J. Shohan, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Responds to Roemer’s complaint about SCAP pricing of Japanese silk textiles.
subfiles.summary: Refers Roemer to Nitze’s earlier reply and says SCAP is responsible for pricing decisions.

subfiles.title: Industrial Commission reply to Charles J. Shohan
subfiles.about: Renews the commission’s claim that Japanese woven silk is sold below fair competitive prices.
subfiles.summary: Roemer says the commission seeks a price adjustment and has supplied supporting evidence to SCAP. He requests reassurance before a silk industry committee meeting scheduled for January 12.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on responsibility for Japanese export prices
subfiles.from: Charles J. Shohan, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Directs Roemer’s further pricing evidence to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: States that SCAP considers Japanese silk textile exports fairly priced and holds primary responsibility for export prices.

subfiles.title: Draft or alternate text of State Department reply to Roemer
subfiles.about: Presents an alternate version of the reply on SCAP’s Japanese silk textile prices.
subfiles.summary: Repeats that SCAP finds the prices fair and asks Roemer to send further evidence there.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1: Increased Prices for Japanese Silk
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a SCAP release announcing increased Japanese raw silk prices.
subfiles.summary: Reports higher 1949 prices, assortment discounts, and continued 1948 prices for SCAP’s New York stocks.

subfiles.title: SCAP press release: Increase Price for Japanese Silk
subfiles.about: Announces 1949 floor prices and sales terms for Japanese raw silk.
subfiles.summary: Tables compare 1948 prices with higher 1949 floor prices by grade and specify two discounted 300 bale assortments. United States stocks remain available at 1948 prices through March 31, 1949.

subfiles.title: Filing or routing page
subfiles.about: Contains a file reference and office routing marks.
subfiles.summary: Sparse filing page bearing the reference 894.6552/2-249.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of embassy reports from Praha and Warsaw
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge of the American Mission, London
subfiles.about: Encloses copies of reports from the American embassies in Praha and Warsaw.
subfiles.summary: Refers to earlier Department telegrams and forwards two embassy reports; the page gives no subject for the reports.
